Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas · Conversation, family & daily routines

go verb

leave, go away

also go away, leave, go off, be off, go away!, shoo, scram, off with you

classical

Hor. Ep. 2.2.215: tempus abīre tibi est
Plaut. Aul. 89: abī intrō

abeō, abīre, abiī, abitum

verb, irregular (ab + eō)

go away, leave

Abī! is “go away!”, or kindly “off you go”; abī intrō, “go inside”. With ab or ex and the place or person left, or with the supine of an errand (abī deambulātum, Ter. Haut. 587).

Other words

  • discēdō, discēdere, discessī, discessum — go away, depart (from a place or a person)

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Plaut. Asin. 251 (Lewis & Short); Cic. Att. 7.2 (Lewis & Short)

    Lewis & Short: “most frequently in all periods”, with ab or ex.

  • apage — away with you! (to a person or a thing)

    interjection · also used · classical · Plaut. Amph. 580: apage tē ā mē (Lewis & Short)

    (vōx cōmica: Plaut., Ter.; numquam apud Cic. (Lewis & Short))

    Also “no thanks, away with it!”: apage, nōn placet mē (Plaut. Amph. 310, in Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • lūsistī satis, ēdistī satis atque bibistī; tempus abīre tibi est

    you have played enough, eaten and drunk enough: it is time for you to goHor. Ep. 2.2.214–215

  • abī intrō, occlūde jānuam. jam ego hīc erō.

    Go inside and shut the door. I’ll be back in a moment.Plaut. Aul. 89

  • St! tacē atque abī.

    Shh! Be quiet and off you go.Plaut. Cas. 148

See also go, departure, set out, leave me alone!, goodbye, safe journey, away, bah!.
